content: Perihepatitis refers to the inflammation of the serous or peritoneal lining that surrounds the liver. This condition is frequently associated with inflammatory disorders of the female upper genital tract, collectively referred to as pelvic inflammatory disease (PID). Patients with perihepatitis may experience sharp pain localized to the right upper quadrant of the abdomen. One notable complication of perihepatitis is the development of Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome, which involves inflammation of the liver capsule and surrounding peritoneum. The most common bacterial pathogens responsible for perihepatitis are Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae, both of which are sexually transmitted infections.
